words.def: Used to add more information that supports what you have already said.
words.note: Furthermore is used to add another important point. It is more formal than also.

col.p_ar: علاوة على ذلك، من المهم أن
col.en: The computer is slow. *Furthermore*, it is important to check its memory.
The software is outdated. *Furthermore*, we need to update the operating system.
The job requires experience. *Furthermore*, there is a technical test.

words.def: Used to introduce a different or opposite point of view.
words.note: On the other hand is commonly used to compare two different sides of a situation.

col.p: on the one hand ... *on the other hand*
col.en: On the one hand, working remotely saves time. *On the other hand*, it can feel lonely.

col.p: *on the other hand*, it can be
col.p_ar: من ناحية أخرى، يمكن أن يكون
col.en: This laptop is cheap. *On the other hand*, it can be difficult to upgrade.
Some people prefer Windows. *On the other hand*, some people prefer Linux.

words.def: Used to introduce a result or consequence of something.
words.note: Consequently is more formal than so. It connects a cause with its result.

col.en: The server stopped working. *Consequently*, we had to restart it.
The company lost several customers. *Consequently*, its profits decreased.
I forgot my password. *Consequently*, I couldn't log in.

words.def: Used to give a specific example of something.
words.note: For instance and for example have almost the same meaning and are commonly used in everyday English.

col.en: You can learn technical skills. *For instance*, you can practice using virtual machines.
Some operating systems are free. *For instance*, Linux is available without a license fee.
You can improve your English. *For instance*, if you practice speaking every day, you will become more confident.

words.def: Used to describe something happening while another thing is happening.
words.note: Meanwhile connects two activities happening around the same time.

col.en: The computer is restarting. *Meanwhile*, I'm going to check the network.
The manager is checking the issue. *Meanwhile*, the team is preparing a report.
Your application is downloading. *Meanwhile*, you can read the instructions.

words.def: Used to add another piece of information.
words.note: Additionally is commonly used in formal writing and presentations. In everyday conversation, also or plus is often more natural.

col.en: We need a new computer. *Additionally*, we need a reliable internet connection.
The course teaches Excel. *Additionally*, it covers Power BI.
You can save your files online. *Additionally*, you can share them with your team.

words.def: Used when two or more things happen together or when two ideas are true together.
words.note: At the same time can describe simultaneous actions or introduce a contrasting point.

col.p: do two things *at the same time*
col.en: I can listen to music and study vocabulary *at the same time*.
I understand the problem. *At the same time*, I need more information.
You can use both applications *at the same time*.

words.def: Used to describe the final result or the most important point after considering everything.
words.note: Ultimately is often used when explaining the final outcome of a process or decision.

col.en: *Ultimately*, it depends on your budget and your needs.
*Ultimately*, we decided to replace the old computer.
*Ultimately*, the goal is to help users solve their technical problems.

words.def: Used to introduce the result of an action or situation.
words.note: As a result is commonly used to explain what happened because of something else.

col.en: I missed the bus. *As a result*, I arrived late.
The update failed. *As a result*, the system became unstable.
The computer shut down *as a result of* a power failure.

words.def: Used to add another person, thing, or activity to what has already been mentioned.
words.note: As well as means in addition to. It is often used to connect two things in the same sentence.

col.en: I study English *as well as* French.
She works full-time *as well as* studying at university.
The job requires communication skills *as well as* the ability to solve technical problems.
